newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan traders cheer stock-index futures.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan traders cheer stock-index futures.

text.p: Taiwan futures traders cheered the government's decision to legalise trading in offshore Taiwan stock-index futures on Wednesday, saying they planned to launch promotions to boost the new market.
"The stock-index futures is a lucrative market, especially since Taiwan's main stock market is booming right now," Eugene Chang, president of Taiwan International Futures Corp, told Reuters.
The liberalisation, announced by the finance ministry, requires cabinet approval which futures traders expect by June 1.
"Once the cabinet give its final approval, futures firms will start to promote and educate Taiwan investors to trade the index futures," Chang said by telephone.
Taiwan stock market's daily trading volume has averaged well above T$100 billion (US$3.6 billion) in recent months, and futures dealers said some investors would use the futures index to hedge risk.
"The index future's trading can be very active even if only a portion of Taiwan investors use the index futures to hedge," Chang said.
Analysts have estimated Taiwan stock-index futures trading could pour T$50 billion a month into offshore markets in Singapore and Chicago.
The Chicago Mercantile Exchange and Singapore International Monetary Exchange launched futures contracts linked to Taiwan's stock market in January.

Taiwan futures houses are already allowed to offer a wide range of major overseas futures contracts, but to date the CME and SIMEX futures were the only contracts linked directly to Taiwan's market performance.
Local investors were forbidden to trade the CME and SIMEX through local futures brokerage houses.
The government has traditionally been leery of futures, regarding them as high-risk financial instruments all but indistinguishable from gambling.
But the launching of CME and SIMEX futures have increased pressure on Taiwan to open its own futures exchange, which some officials said could come as early as October.
Officials said they expected the first item to be traded on the new exchange to be contracts linked to the benchmark TAIEX index of the main Taiwan Stock Exchange.
